questions.question: An arithmetic sequence has first term u_1 = 5 and common difference d = 3 . What is the sum of the first 20 terms, S_20 ?
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 1.2: Arithmetic Sequences and Series

questions.question: The first term of a geometric sequence is u_1 = 12 and the sum to infinity is S_∞ = 36 . What is the common ratio r ?
questions.explanation: For an infinite convergent geometric series with |r| < 1 , S_∞ = (u_1/1 - r) . Substituting values: 36 = (12/1 - r) ⇒ 1 - r = (12/36) = (1/3) ⇒ r = 1 - (1/3) = (2/3) .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 1.3: Geometric Sequences and Series

questions.question: If log_3(x) + log_3(x - 2) = 1 , what is the value of x ?
questions.explanation: Combine logarithms: log_3[x(x - 2)] = 1 ⇒ x(x - 2) = 3^1 ⇒ x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0 . Factoring gives (x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 . Because the domain of log_3(x) requires x > 2 , x = -1 is rejected as extraneous, so x = 3 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 1.5: Laws of Logarithms

questions.question: What is the coefficient of x^4 in the expansion of (2x - 1)^6 ?
questions.explanation: The general term is T_r+1 = C(6, r) (2x)^6-r (-1)^r . For the x^4 term, 6 - r = 4 ⇒ r = 2 . Term = C(6, 2) (2x)^4 (-1)^2 = 15 × 16x^4 × 1 = 240x^4 . Thus the coefficient is 240.
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 1.9: Binomial Theorem

questions.subtopic: Topic 1: Number & Algebra (Complex Numbers in Polar Form)
questions.question: Let z = 1 + i√(3) . What is the exact value of z^6 using de Moivre's theorem?
questions.explanation: Modulus r = √(1^2 + (\sqrt3))^2 = 2 . Argument θ = arctan(√(3)/1) = (π/3) . In polar form, z = 2 e^iπ/3 . By de Moivre's theorem, z^6 = 2^6 e^i(6 × π/3) = 64 e^i(2π) = 64(cos 2π + isin 2π) = 64(1 + 0) = 64 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 1.13: Complex Numbers (HL)

questions.subtopic: Topic 1: Number & Algebra (Proof by Mathematical Induction)
questions.question: When proving by mathematical induction that 4^n - 1 is divisible by 3 for all integers n ≥ 1 , what is the inductive step algebraic expression for 4^k+1 - 1 ?
questions.explanation: 4^k+1 - 1 = 4 · 4^k - 1 = 4(4^k - 1 + 1) - 1 = 4(4^k - 1) + 4 - 1 = 4(4^k - 1) + 3 . Since 4^k - 1 = 3M by induction hypothesis, 4(3M) + 3 = 3(4M + 1) , which is divisible by 3.
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 1.15: Proof by Induction (HL)

questions.question: Let f(x) = (2x + 1/x - 3) for x ≠ 3 . What is the inverse function f^-1(x) ?
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 2.2: Composite and Inverse Functions

questions.question: The graph of y = f(x) is transformed to y = 3f(x - 2) + 5 . Which sequence of geometric transformations describes this change?
options: Translation by vector ( 2 , 5 ) and vertical stretch with scale factor 3
Translation by vector ( -2 , 5 ) and horizontal stretch with scale factor 3
Translation by vector ( 2 , -5 ) and vertical stretch with scale factor (1/3)
Reflection in the x-axis followed by translation by vector ( 2 , 5 )
questions.explanation: f(x - 2) translates the graph 2 units to the right (vector ( 2 , 0 ) ). Multiplying by 3 stretches the graph vertically by scale factor 3. Adding 5 translates the graph 5 units upward (vector ( 0 , 5 ) ). Total translation vector is ( 2 , 5 ) .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 2.3: Transformations of Graphs

questions.question: For what values of k does the line y = 2x + k touch the parabola y = x^2 - 4x + 5 at exactly one point?
questions.explanation: Set the equations equal: x^2 - 4x + 5 = 2x + k ⇒ x^2 - 6x + (5 - k) = 0 . For tangency (one intersection), the discriminant \Delta = b^2 - 4ac = 0 . (-6)^2 - 4(1)(5 - k) = 0 ⇒ 36 - 20 + 4k = 0 ⇒ 16 + 4k = 0 ⇒ 4k = -16 ⇒ k = -4 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 2.6: Quadratic Functions

questions.question: What are the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of the rational function f(x) = (4x - 7/2x + 6) ?
options: Vertical asymptote: x = -3 ; Horizontal asymptote: y = 2
Vertical asymptote: x = 3 ; Horizontal asymptote: y = 4
Vertical asymptote: x = -3 ; Horizontal asymptote: y = -(7/6)
Vertical asymptote: x = 2 ; Horizontal asymptote: y = -3
questions.explanation: The vertical asymptote occurs where the denominator is zero: 2x + 6 = 0 ⇒ x = -3 . The horizontal asymptote is the limit as x \to ±∞ : \lim_x \to ∞ (4x - 7/2x + 6) = (4/2) = 2 ⇒ y = 2 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 2.8: Rational Functions

questions.question: What is the complete solution set to the equation |2x - 5| = x + 1 ?
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 2.12: Modulus Functions (HL)

questions.question: Which of the following functions satisfies f(-x) = -f(x) for all x \in ℝ (is an odd function)?
questions.explanation: f(-x) = (-x)^3 + sin(-x) = -x^3 - sin(x) = -(x^3 + sin x) = -f(x) . Since f(-x) = -f(x) , the function is odd with rotational symmetry of 180° about the origin.
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 2.13: Odd and Even Functions (HL)

questions.subtopic: Topic 3: Geometry & Trigonometry (Radian Measure & Arc Length)
questions.question: A circle of radius r = 6 cm has a sector with an arc length of 4π cm . What is the area of this sector?
questions.explanation: Arc length l = rθ ⇒ 4π = 6θ ⇒ θ = (4π/6) = (2π/3) rad . Area of sector A = (1/2) r^2 θ = (1/2) (6)^2 ≤ft((2π/3)\right) = (1/2)(36)≤ft((2π/3)\right) = 18 × (2π/3) = 12π cm^2 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 3.1: Radians, Arcs and Sectors

questions.question: Given that cosθ = (3/5) and (3π/2) < θ < 2π (Quadrant IV), what is the exact value of sin(2θ) ?
questions.explanation: In Quadrant IV, sine is negative: sinθ = -√(1 - cos^2θ) = -√(1 - 9/25) = -(4/5) . Using the double angle identity sin(2θ) = 2sinθcosθ : sin(2θ) = 2≤ft(-(4/5)\right)≤ft((3/5)\right) = -(24/25) .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 3.6: Double Angle Identities

questions.question: How many solutions exist for the equation 2cos^2 x - cos x - 1 = 0 in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π ?
questions.explanation: Factoring gives (2cos x + 1)(cos x - 1) = 0 . From cos x = 1 , we have x = 0 and x = 2π . From cos x = -(1/2) , we have x = (2π/3) and x = (4π/3) . All four values lie in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π . Thus, there are exactly 4 solutions.
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 3.5: Solving Trigonometric Equations

questions.subtopic: Topic 3: Geometry & Trigonometry (Scalar Product of Vectors)
questions.question: For which value of p are the vectors a = ( 3 , -2 , 4 ) and b = ( 2 , p , -4 ) perpendicular?
questions.explanation: Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular if and only if their scalar (dot) product is zero: a · b = 0 ⇒ (3)(2) + (-2)(p) + (4)(-4) = 0 ⇒ 6 - 2p - 16 = 0 ⇒ -10 - 2p = 0 ⇒ 2p = -10 ⇒ p = -5 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 3.13: Scalar Product (HL)

questions.subtopic: Topic 3: Geometry & Trigonometry (Vector Equation of a Line)
questions.question: A line L passes through point A(1, -2, 3) with direction vector d = ( 2 , 1 , -1 ) . Which of the following points lies on line L ?
questions.explanation: Vector equation: r = ( 1 , -2 , 3 ) + \lambda ( 2 , 1 , -1 ) . For \lambda = 2 : x = 1 + 2(2) = 5 , y = -2 + 2(1) = 0 , z = 3 + 2(-1) = 1 . Point (5, 0, 1) lies on the line.
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 3.14: Vector Equations of Lines (HL)

questions.question: What is the exact value of cos(75^°) = cos≤ft((5π/12)\right) ?
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 3.6: Compound Angle Identities

questions.question: Events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5 . What is P(A \cup B) ?
questions.explanation: For independent events, P(A \cap B) = P(A) × P(B) = (0.4)(0.5) = 0.20 . Using the addition rule: P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = 0.4 + 0.5 - 0.20 = 0.70 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 4.5: Independent Events

questions.question: A discrete random variable X has the probability distribution where P(X=1) = 0.2 , P(X=2) = 0.5 , and P(X=3) = 0.3 . What is the expected value E(X) ?
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 4.7: Discrete Random Variables

questions.question: A fair six-sided die is rolled 5 times. Let X be the number of times a '6' is rolled ( X \sim B(5, 1/6) ). What is the probability of rolling exactly two sixes, P(X = 2) ?
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 4.8: Binomial Distribution

questions.question: A continuous random variable X \sim N(50, 16) has mean \mu = 50 and standard deviation \sigma = 4 . What is the z-score corresponding to x = 58 ?
questions.explanation: Standardized score formula: z = (x - \mu/\sigma) . Variance \sigma^2 = 16 ⇒ \sigma = 4 . Thus, z = (58 - 50/4) = (8/4) = +2.0 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 4.9: Normal Distribution

questions.question: Given that P(A) = 0.6 , P(B) = 0.3 , and P(A \cap B) = 0.18 , what is P(A | B) ?
questions.explanation: By definition, P(A | B) = (P(A \cap B)/P(B)) = (0.18/0.3) = 0.60 . Note that P(A | B) = P(A) , proving A and B are independent.
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 4.6: Conditional Probability

questions.subtopic: Topic 4: Statistics & Probability (Variance of Linear Transformation)
questions.question: A random variable X has variance Var(X) = 9 . What is the variance of Y = 3 - 2X ?
questions.explanation: By properties of variance for linear transformation Y = aX + b : Var(aX + b) = a^2 Var(X) . Here a = -2 and b = 3 : Var(3 - 2X) = (-2)^2 Var(X) = 4 × 9 = 36 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 4.14: Linear Combinations of Variables (HL)

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = x^2 e^3x with respect to x ?
questions.explanation: Using the product rule (uv)' = u'v + uv' with u = x^2 ⇒ u' = 2x and v = e^3x ⇒ v' = 3e^3x : f'(x) = 2x e^3x + x^2 (3e^3x) = x e^3x(2 + 3x) .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 5.6: Product and Chain Rules

questions.question: What is the equation of the tangent line to the curve y = x^3 - 2x + 4 at the point where x = 1 ?
questions.explanation: When x = 1 , y = 1^3 - 2(1) + 4 = 3 . The point of tangency is (1, 3) . Derivative (dy/dx) = 3x^2 - 2 . At x = 1 , gradient m = 3(1)^2 - 2 = 1 . Tangent equation: y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) ⇒ y - 3 = 1(x - 1) ⇒ y = x + 2 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 5.7: Tangents and Normals

questions.question: For the function f(x) = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x - 3 , what are the coordinates and nature of the local maximum point?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 6x^2 - 18x + 12 = 6(x^2 - 3x + 2) = 6(x - 1)(x - 2) . Stationary points at x = 1 and x = 2 . Second derivative f''(x) = 12x - 18 . At x = 1 : f''(1) = 12 - 18 = -6 < 0 ⇒ Local Maximum. Value f(1) = 2(1)^3 - 9(1)^2 + 12(1) - 3 = 2 . Local maximum is at (1, 2) .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 5.8: Local Extrema and Curve Sketching

questions.question: A particle moves along a straight line such that its velocity at time t ≥ 0 is v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 m/s . At what times is the particle instantaneously at rest?
questions.explanation: A particle is instantaneously at rest when v(t) = 0 . Set 3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 0 ⇒ 3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 0 ⇒ 3(t - 1)(t - 3) = 0 ⇒ t = 1 s and t = 3 s .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 5.9: Kinematics

questions.question: What is the exact value of the definite integral ∫_1^4 ≤ft(2x - (1/√(x))\right) dx ?
questions.explanation: Rewrite integrand as 2x - x^-1/2 . Antiderivative: ≤ft[ x^2 - \fracx^1/21/2 \right]_1^4 = ≤ft[ x^2 - 2√(x) \right]_1^4 . At x = 4 : 4^2 - 2√(4) = 16 - 4 = 12 . At x = 1 : 1^2 - 2√(1) = 1 - 2 = -1 . Value = 12 - (-1) = 13 .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 5.10: Definite Integrals and Area

questions.question: What is the indefinite integral ∫ 2x cos(x^2) dx ?
questions.explanation: Let u = x^2 ⇒ du = 2x dx . Substituting: ∫ cos(u) du = sin(u) + C = sin(x^2) + C .
questions.citation: IB Mathematics AA Guide — Topic 5.11: Integration by Substitution
